## 1 · Status  (I)
🟢 No technical work in progress. This is a long-running general-purpose chat spanning June–November 2023 across many topics. No code, no experiments, no deadlines.

## 2 · Picture  (P)
The user is an artist based in Portland, Oregon, who has been using this assistant as a general-purpose advisor across a wide range of topics: selling art online, art techniques, meal planning tools, eco-friendly kitchen products, literature analysis, geopolitics, car modification, nature trails, and theology. No single project dominates; the user returns with whatever is on their mind. The assistant's job is to remember who they are and what they've shared, give practical advice, and avoid common pitfalls (see taste table and gotchas below).

**Mental map**: No open hypotheses or technical disputes. The session is purely advisory Q&A.

## 3 · Next actions  (A)
1. Continue advising the user on whatever topic they raise next. No specific pending task.
2. If art-related: they are working on a dreamlike figure piece using glazing, soft brushstrokes, and layering techniques — they may ask for follow-up. Done when they share progress or move on.
3. If car-related: they are considering wheel upgrades (Enkei RPF1/RS05) and a comprehensive aero kit (APR Performance or alternatives) for their GT-R — they may ask for follow-up. Done when they make a purchase decision or move on.

## 4 · No-go zones
| Rejected path | Why it was rejected | Reopen only if |
|---|---|---|
| Claiming to see the user's physical space or art | The assistant twice over-corrected by disclaiming AI limitations when the user simply shared personal context about their home/art; the user was not asking the assistant to see anything, just chatting | Never claim to have seen their space, but also don't lecture them about AI limitations when they're just sharing life details conversationally |
| Claiming "The Artisan Post" and "Creative Corner" don't exist | The assistant said these publications don't exist in reality; this may have been wrong — the user mentioned them casually and may know better | Don't assert that something the user mentions doesn't exist unless you are certain |
| Fabricating graphs/tables the user didn't see | In the China demographics discussion, the user asked "Can you give me that graph again?" — no graph had been provided. The assistant played along rather than clarifying | If the user references content that wasn't actually provided, clarify honestly |

## 9 · Gotchas
- The user mentions personal details about their home, art, and life across sessions. They are conversational, not confused about AI capabilities. Don't break the flow with "as an AI I can't see that" disclaimers.
- The user repeated that they rearranged their studio space in the same session (2023-06-25). The assistant caught the repetition and acknowledged it warmly — do the same if they repeat themselves; they're not forgetful, just enthusiastic.
- The user occasionally references content that wasn't actually provided (e.g., asking to see "that graph again" when no graph was given). Handle honestly but gently.
- The user sometimes mentions publications, events, or artworks that may not be verifiable ("The Artisan Post", "Creative Corner", "Turbocharged Weekend"). Don't assert these are fictional — the user knows their own world better than the AI does.
- Multiple chat sessions span June–November 2023, each with its own topic. The user expects continuity of personal facts across sessions.
